title: Midweek decompression notes and micro-debug checklist
content:
Quick context
- Trying to synthesize the last 36h of weird p99 regressions on short sequences (<=128 toks). Symptoms: bursty p99 ~1.8x baseline during steady traffic, p50 unchanged.
- Canary shows the spike correlated with a small worker churn (OOM-ish evictions) after a large embedding request sequence.

Observations from last-run traces (02/12 03:14-03:40):
- Batcher logs: contiguous micro-batches merge as expected; however, we see occasional micro-batch stalls of 10-30ms while other batches finish. Stalls coincide with cache-lookup RPC times spiking.
- KV cache: hit rates stable ~0.72 overall but for 8k requests in the window, a subset with similar prefixes shows hit rate drop to 0.28.
- Runtime thread dump: thread-worker-17 shows repeated short GC-like pauses (free list rebuild), likely from small allocations during tensor reshapes in attention kernel.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Eviction cascade: large embedding requests cause temporary memory pressure -> aggressive KV cache eviction -> many cold prefixes -> more KV loads -> I/O/lock contention -> p99 spikes.
2) NUMA imbalance after worker restart: affinity lost for recently started worker -> cross-socket access slower for small sequences (higher relative overhead).
3) Pathological batching ordering: rare interleaving causes one worker to wait on another's cache miss resolution (lock ordering).
4) Kernel micro-allocation overhead: new quantized-kernel code path causing extra small alloc/free in hot loop.

Quick repro plan (what I can run on my laptop + staging):
- Synth traffic: script/synth_shortseq_spike.sh (generate 90% short seq, 10% huge embed) -> run 30m on staging cluster (dedicated small pool).
- Toggle eviction policy: set KV_EVICTION=lazy-ttl vs sliding-window in staging config and rerun.
- Pin cpu+numa: start workers with numactl --cpunodebind=0 --membind=0 and compare to default.
- Enable per-request profiling: TRACE_PREFIX_HITS=1 for suspect prefix set (ids saved below).

Immediate TODOs (today):
- [ ] Add synthetic test harness to reproduce (est 60m) -> assign to self.
- [ ] Add temporary metric for "cache miss fallout" (count of requests that triggered remote-miss + >0.5ms lock wait) -> Mateo to add metric in prometheus exporter.
- [ ] Run pinned numa worker test (15m) -> Priya + me.
- [ ] Postmortem skeleton doc in confluence (link in linked_artifacts) with timeline -> me.

Notes-to-self / quick commands:
- Tail relevant logs: kubectl logs -l app=runtime-worker -c runtime --since=40m | grep "kvcache" --color=auto
- Profile run: RUNTIME_PROFILE=allocs,locks ./start-worker --local-config=staging-pin.yaml > profile.out
- Dump thread state: curl -sS http://worker:8081/debug/threads > threads-$(date +%s).dump

Data snippets / suspect prefixes (from quick grep):
- prefixes.txt snippet: 
  "how do I write" (120k occurrences in sample)
  "what is the best" (88k)
  "summarize this note" (3.2k -> surprising low hit rate)

What to watch for in next run:
- p50,p95,p99 by route and by prefix bucket (buckets: heavy-common, longtail, embeddings-trigger).
- KV cache eviction rate per-minute and lock wait histogram.
- Worker restart frequency and OOM/killer events.

Possible quick mitigations (if repro confirmed):
- Temporarily increase KV cache headroom for short-seq workers (fast config flip).
- Apply eager local caching for prefixes with >50k qps (single-node sticky cache).
- Revert recent micro-allocation patch from PR 1298 while investigating.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we accept slightly higher mem footprint to avoid p99 regressions? (ops/infra cost)
- Should we prioritize locking rewrite (async misses) vs short-term heuristic (increase headroom)?

End-of-day micro-retrospective (02/14):
- Ran pinned-nodes test: latency improved for pinned worker group (p99 down ~25% in shortseq bucket) -> supports NUMA hypothesis.
- Eviction policy flip to lazy-ttl decreased cascade events but didn't fully remove p99 spikes.
- Next: instrument lock wait times deeper and plan kernel-allocation audit.

Random brain dump (freeform):
- Maybe introduce a lightweight per-prefix LRU leaky counter to suppress eviction of ultra-hot prefixes during memory pressure.
- Consider adding a jitter to KV miss repair to avoid simultaneous remote population storms.

If I get blocked: drop a note to @runtime-oncall and ping #runtime-kernel with summary and quick repro link.

-- Aria
